sections.history: No recollection of the event. Witnessed by wife: went quiet, then left arm jerking for a few seconds, followed by generalised stiffening and shaking lasting about 2 minutes (wife initially estimated 5 minutes, then confirmed 2 by the clock). Perioral cyanosis, lateral tongue bite, urinary incontinence. Post-ictal confusion for about 20 minutes. Preceded by sleep deprivation after four consecutive night shifts. No alcohol that day; a few pints at weekends. No drug use. No previous seizures, myoclonic jerks or absences. No head injury or CNS infection. No family history of epilepsy. Works as a warehouse supervisor. Drives.
sections.medications_allergies: No regular medications. No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Neurological examination normal. CT head in ED normal. Bloods normal.
sections.impression: First generalised tonic-clonic seizure, possibly of focal onset (left arm, suggesting right hemisphere), provoked in part by sleep deprivation.
sections.plan: MRI brain (epilepsy protocol) and EEG. No antiseizure medication at present. Must not drive; patient to inform the DVLA (usually 6 months off driving after a first seizure). Safety advice: showers not baths, no swimming alone, avoid heights, regular sleep. Seizure first aid explained to wife. Clinic review with results in about 6 weeks.
sections.safety_netting: If a further seizure: recovery position, time it, call 999 if longer than 5 minutes or injured.
